memo.verdict: Neutral. Park at this price (3236p, 2026-09-25) with a watch level. Progress to Early-Stage if either the price falls to about 2,880p (where the modal path clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months) or the FY2026 print on 23 February 2027 shows shared-site utilisation above 95 percent of 2019 with price/mix flat or better and an H2 2026 margin above 18.5 percent, which would move the cleared-branch odds from 40 percent toward 60 percent and the eighteen-month return toward a B at the current price. Conviction: medium on the direction of the earnings, low-to-medium on the return, because the swing factor is the multiple. The park rule is not triggered: management C, business quality B, predictability B, trackability C, all clear of D. Not an invalidation.
case: - What the case is: a cause-for-concern-clearing case in a high-quality business, not a compounder and not a demand inflection. The margin fell from 24.8 percent in 2021 to 17.2 percent in 2024 because destocking emptied eleven shared manufacturing sites while the cost base and a pharma capacity build ran ahead of sales. The clearing is half self-help (the £100m programme, £46m delivered by H1 2026, run by a new chief financial officer) and half cyclical (utilisation back to 93 percent of the 2019 baseline, crop destocking over, premium beauty demand strong).

- The internal change is real, controllable and evidenced in delivery: the programme upscaled from £40m to £100m; minimum order values; CrodaOn at 18 percent of customers; 30 percent of SKUs reviewed; globalised procurement; finance shared services; capex to 4.9 percent of sales; the 2026 bonus 90 percent on constant-currency adjusted operating profit and the share plan carrying a 25 percent ROIC weighting. No screen red flag: no caretaker chief executive, not a 'PowerPoint transformation', no crown-jewel sale, no empire-building (bolt-ons under £10m), leverage 1.4 times, no debt-funded buyback.

- The external forces net to a mild tailwind with wide dispersion and no sector-level explosion: Beauty Actives +27 percent in Q2 2026 (+19 percent H1), Consumer Care +13.5 percent in Q2 (+8.3 percent H1), Crop Protection +5 percent in Q2 after −8 percent in Q1, Pharma Ingredients +7 percent H1; against that Pharma Solutions −17 percent H1 2026 (recovery guided on order books, not shown), Fragrances & Flavours slowed to 8 percent from mid-teens, sterling a £20m headwind, competition tightening in commoditised surfactants and aroma chemicals (Croda cut prices in the least-differentiated 20 percent of Beauty Care to recapture 40 percent of lost US volume; Chinese generics up to 33 percent of Brazilian crop volumes; Privi's 54,000 tonnes of aroma capacity). Macro D: sterling translation acts on Croda more than the universe. The activist Standard Industries pushes for deeper cuts, site rationalisation and a Seed Enhancement disposal (5 percent of sales).
counter_case: - The strongest case against, the volume-led false friend (the risks research's winning hypothesis; the change-forces research's 'fatal circular dependency'; Deutsche Bank and Jefferies): to fill the shared sites Croda must sell low-value surfactants and cut prices in its least-differentiated lines, so volume recovers, utilisation rises, and the gross margin and mix erode; fixed costs rise £15m a year and depreciation £10m as the pharma assets complete; the £100m programme is absorbed by inflation; the margin stalls at 18 to 19 percent; consensus' 20.4 percent is cut; and at 16 times a lower earnings base the shares are worth 2,500 to 2,800p (Jefferies' 2,500p; the dashboard sector's 14 times).

- The evidence for it: price/mix −3.0 percent in FY2025 against volume +9.6 percent; divisional EBIT 14 percent below consensus in H1 2026 on negative operating leverage; organic sales +7 percent with flat EBIT margins in 2025; administrative expenses from 18 to 26 percent of sales; ROIC 8.2 percent; Industrial Specialties retained solely to fill shared sites; the 2022 blunt price hikes that lost share; turnarounds that prioritise utilisation over price fail 40 percent of the time on the sector base rate; nearly half of specialty turnarounds fail on longer-than-expected inventory cycles; Lamar built ahead of demand and idle.
triggers: - Progress triggers: the price at about 2,880p (modal path clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months); or the FY2026 print (23 February 2027) showing utilisation above 95 percent of 2019 with price/mix flat or better and an H2 2026 margin above 18.5 percent, moving the cleared-branch odds toward 60 percent and the rating of the 'Investment Case' to B. A print with utilisation above 95 percent and price/mix positive would move the utilisation odds to 70 percent and the re-rating branch to about 55 percent.

- Alarm levels: shared-site utilisation below 90 percent at the FY2026 print; FY2026 savings below £20m (watch below £35m); administrative expenses rising as a share of sales; price/mix worse than −2 percent while volume grows; H2 2026 margin below 18 percent (the path needs about 18.3 percent in H2 for 18.0 percent in FY2026); Pharma Solutions failing to recover in H2 2026; a second half-year of working-capital outflow (watch: net working capital days rising year on year); the 24-month-forward multiple below 14 times with earnings unchanged (mark-to-market alarm); Consumer Care organic growth below 8 percent in Q3 2026 (watch).
- Invalidate level: Consumer Care operating margin below 17 percent.

- Watch series: utilisation against 100 percent of 2019; savings against £35m for FY2026; Consumer Care organic growth against 8 percent; price/mix during volume recovery; Consumer Care operating margin; Pharma Solutions H2 2026 sales against the H1 fall; net working capital days; free cash flow to sales against 12 percent; Malaysian crude palm oil; GBP/USD and GBP/EUR; Brazilian agrochemical imports; prestige beauty sell-through; Givaudan, Symrise and DSM-Firmenich prints (a Symrise or DSM-Firmenich margin warning would hit the multiple regardless of Croda's numbers); Standard Industries' holding; succession announcements.

- Near steps: the Q3 2026 trading update (October); evidence on the H2 Pharma Solutions recovery; the Q2 price increases annualising; the FY2026 results with the £35m savings test. Mid steps: the FY2027 savings tranche (£25m) and the £100m run-rate by end-2027; ROIC toward 10 percent; a possible special cash return by 2027; activist-driven portfolio steps; Kerabio and ceramide scale-up. Far steps: the FY2028 target year; the 2028 EU microplastics seed-coating ban.

- What would change the record's mind on each turning point: FY2026 savings below £20m or administrative expenses rising (the programme); utilisation below 90 percent or price/mix worse than −2 percent (utilisation); an H2 2026 margin below 18 percent (the 20 percent margin); a peer de-rating on a Symrise or Givaudan warning (the re-rating's second condition); a second half-year of working-capital outflow (cash conversion).
